subject: Novaforge dedicated capacity roadmap & regional selection
messages:
From: Ethan Wu <ethan.wu@novaforge.com>

Date: Wed, 29 Apr 2026 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity needs and regional constraints

Hi Aditya / Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Novaforge wants to move forward with a dedicated GPU pool for inference in our EU region (initial traffic profile attached). We have a few constraints:
- Data residency in Frankfurt (DE) required for EU customers.
- Peak inference bursts around product launches (3x baseline for ~2 hours, unpredictable).
- Our model footprint: 1x 13B for realtime + 2x 7B for background batch embeddings.

Can Redwood outline a proposed capacity plan (pool sizing, autoscale/burst policy, fallback region) and any documentation you need from our infra team? Attaching a short spec and traffic export.

Prefer a kickoff call Thu 30th if possible.

Attachments: novaforge_infra_requirements.pdf, regional_traffic_export.json

—Ethan
Ethan Wu
Head of Platform, Novaforge

Hi Ethan — really appreciate the clear brief and the traffic export. Monica and I reviewed the high-level ask and sketched a first-pass plan.

Short answer: we can provision a Frankfurt-only dedicated pool with automatic burst capacity and a failover to Dublin (secondary EU region). Proposed next steps:
1) Kickoff meeting Thu 30 Apr — 30 min to align constraints and SLOs (we'll send calendar).
2) We will share a "provisioning roadmap" doc with pool sizing + autoscale guardrails (v1 attached).
3) Karthik will validate the autoscale safety limits against your peak profile and propose a burst policy (duration cap, cooldown, and cost cap).
4) Exchange of infra access: secure runbook for netops (we'll need an ops contact and a short list of permitted IPs).

I attached the provisioning-roadmap-v1.pdf which includes: pool sizing heuristics, warm-start KV cache recommendations, and suggested monitoring dashboards.

Action items for Novaforge before kickoff:
- Confirm preferred kickoff time (we propose Thu 30 Apr 11:00 CEST).
- Share any existing capacity reservations with your cloud provider (region quotas).
- Point of contact for collecting KMS/HSM key policy questions.

I'll loop in Stephanie to start the implementation checklist after the meeting.

Regards,

Folks — forwarding Novaforge note. Key asks: Frankfurt residency, bursty 3x peaks, 1x13B realtime + 2x7B batch embed.

Prep checklist (internal):
- Karthik: Can you draft an autoscale/burst policy that enforces a hard budget cap and automatic fallback after X minutes? Think about: min-warm workers, burst ceiling (in vCPUs/GPU units), and a cooldown window.
- Stephanie: start a short implementation checklist for private networking (VPC peering / SFTP of logs), and confirm the DocuSign / SOW flow for Dedicated contracts.
- Monica: have sales ops share the HubSpot deal (D-20347-NOV) and confirm the billing cadence preference.

Also note: Novaforge mentioned unpredictable bursts; we should propose a short prefix KV cache to reduce token generation on the 13B during launches. Karthik — please include cache warm-up strategy.

Aditya

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Ethan Wu <ethan.wu@novaforge.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Apr 2026 08:41:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity needs and regional constraints

Thanks — quick draft of the burst/autoscale approach below (attaching regional_capacity_matrix.xlsx):

Proposal (vA):
- Baseline pool: 6x A40-equivalent workers (covers steady-state for 1x13B + 2x7B at medium concurrency).
- Burst window: +12 workers available via reserved burst capacity for up to 3 hours per event (sized to handle 3x baseline).
- Hard budget cap: burst spend limited to $X/hour and automatically disables burst if spend > daily cap for two consecutive days.
- Cooldown: automatic scale-down after 25 minutes of sustained <30% CPU utilization.
- Fallback: if FR region unavailable, route to Dublin pool with model variant (quantized 13B) and throttled concurrency.

Cache strategy: maintain a prefix KV cache on 13B workers; pre-warm cache for scheduled launches (we'll expose an API call Novaforge can hit hours prior to an event).

Open implementation questions:
- Do they want burst reserved capacity on contract or on-demand? (contracted burst gives guaranteed headroom).
- KMS/HSM: need confirmation of key management approach; if customer-managed we'll need an onboarding window.

Attaching: regional_capacity_matrix.xlsx (sizing by region / SKU / expected QPS).

-Karthik
Lead Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference
